newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil faces Mercosur flak over import rule change.
newsitem.headline: Brazil faces Mercosur flak over import rule change.

text.p: Brazil came under pressure Monday from its parters in the Mercosur trade bloc who want to be excluded from new measures that restrict import financing.

Paraguay -- currently the president of the four-nation group which also includes Argentina and Uruguay -- sent a letter to Brazil's Foreign Ministry, urging "the swiftest exclusion of Mercosur countries regarding the new ... rules."

Brazil's Central Bank last Tuesday announced restrictions on import financing of under a year, with the aim of preventing importers from benefiting from low international interest rates. The rules apply to goods shipped after March 31.

"Previously (Brazil) applied restrictions to financing of exports to that country, seriously affecting not just Paraguay's exports, but also those of the other Mercosur states," Parguay's letter, signed by Foreign Minister Ruben Melgarejo, said.

Argentine Finance Minister Roque Fernandez was scheduled to arrive in Brazil on Tuesday to discuss the measures with his Brazilian counterpart Pedro Malan and other ministers, a spokesman at the Argentine Embassy said.
Uruguayan Finance Minister Luis Mosca might also visit Brasilia this week to ask for Mercosur exemption from the measures, Uruguayan Ambassador Mario Cesar Fernandez said.

Brazil, by far the biggest market in the bloc, has said it will analyse the requests on a bilateral basis. But Uruguay, like Argentina and Paraguay, want the discussions to take part on a Mercosur-wide level, the ambassador said.

The Brazilian government has defended the new import financing rules, denying there was anything "protectionist" about it. But analysts have said the new rules were designed to help plug Brazil's widening trade deficit.
